seoTitle: Fix WordPress "Can't Provide Secure Connection" Error
metaDescription: Learn how to fix the WordPress SSL error where your site can't provide a secure connection, covering certificate installation, DNS, and mixed content.
intro: The 'This site can't provide a secure connection' error on a WordPress site usually points to an SSL certificate, DNS, or mixed-content problem rather than something wrong with your content. This guide walks through the most common causes and how to fix them so HTTPS works reliably across browsers and devices.

steps.heading: Understand why the error appears
steps.body: This SSL/HTTPS error typically shows up when the SSL certificate isn't installed correctly, the domain isn't pointing properly, mixed-content issues exist, or the hosting configuration is off.

steps.heading: Install or renew your SSL certificate
steps.body: Check with your hosting provider that a valid SSL certificate is installed and not expired, and renew it if necessary.

steps.heading: Force HTTPS across your site
steps.body: Update your WordPress site URL settings and server configuration to force all traffic to load over HTTPS instead of HTTP.

steps.heading: Fix mixed content issues
steps.body: Scan for and update any resources — images, scripts, or links — still loading over HTTP, since these can trigger security warnings even with a valid certificate.

steps.heading: Check DNS and hosting configuration
steps.body: Confirm your domain's DNS records point correctly to your hosting provider, since misconfigured DNS can also cause secure connection failures.

faq.question: Why does the error show on some devices but not others?
faq.answer: This can happen when cached SSL data or DNS records differ between devices, or when mixed content only affects certain browsers' security settings.

faq.question: Do I need to buy an SSL certificate for WordPress?
faq.answer: Many hosts provide free SSL certificates through providers like Let's Encrypt, so a paid certificate usually isn't necessary unless you have specific requirements.

faq.question: What is mixed content and why does it cause errors?
faq.answer: Mixed content happens when a secure HTTPS page still loads some resources over HTTP, which browsers flag as a security risk.

faq.question: Can Cloudflare cause this SSL error?
faq.answer: Yes, an incorrect Cloudflare SSL mode setting can conflict with your origin server's certificate and trigger secure connection errors.
